name: libsigrok
desc: Drivers for logic analyzers and other supported devices
why: Drivers that turn dozens of logic analysers and oscilloscopes into open tools, a door into watching digital signals on real circuits.

brief.what_it_is: libsigrok is a library of device drivers for logic analyzers and other supported test and measurement hardware, according to its Homebrew formula description: "Drivers for logic analyzers and other supported devices." The scout notes say it covers dozens of logic analyzers and oscilloscopes and turns them into open tools for watching digital signals on real circuits. I could not read the homepage or any README, so I have not confirmed the input and output details or the exact device list. This entry rests on the formula description and scout notes alone.
brief.why_it_exists: The only stated purpose is the formula description: supplying drivers for logic analyzers and other supported devices. The scout notes frame it as a way to open up hardware that would otherwise need vendor software. I could not check the author's own framing.
brief.install_notes: Installed via brew install libsigrok, per the formula. The formula lists no executables, so there is no obvious command to run after install. I found no README details on runtimes, hardware, accounts, or first-run steps.
brief.standout: The scout notes describe it as a set of open drivers that make many commercial logic analyzers and oscilloscopes usable from open tools. I could not verify how it compares to similar projects.
brief.status: unknown. The homepage and the GitHub path github.com/sigrok/libsigrok both failed to load, so I found no release date, last commit, or maintenance note.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://sigrok.org/ was unreachable (URLError), and the GitHub fallback returned HTTP 404, so this brief is built from the formula description and scout notes only. No README, command, quote, or device list was read, and the brief makes no claims beyond those two sources. The formula lists no executables.
